job_description_info.job_description:
# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

Its products help customers plan routes and loads, track shipments in real time, and manage delivery notes and customs paperwork. More than 340 freight forwarders across 19 countries use its platform, which processes tens of millions of shipment events daily.

The company’s work supports Europe’s freight and supply chains, with a focus on reducing manual status-chasing and making shipment information more visible. Tessel is growing its engineering team and investing in predictive arrival estimates, reliability and system observability.

Its stated values are **“Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.”** The working culture emphasizes small teams, ownership of services from development through operations, clear and concise design notes, and dedicated time for reliability improvements. Teams work across Antwerp, Poznań and a remote-first engineering group. Tessel also shares technical knowledge through an engineering blog and supports the local Python community.

# Tessel Cargo Software in the news
*(fictional news item – tesselcargo.example/news/series-b)*

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.
# Careers at Tessel Cargo Software
*(fictional careers page – tesselcargo.example/careers)*

## Build the software behind Europe's supply chains

**Engineering at Tessel**
- Stack: Python (FastAPI), Go for a few high-throughput workers, PostgreSQL, Kafka, AWS (EKS, RDS, S3), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry
- Team structure: product teams of 6-8 engineers with an engineering manager and a product manager
- Practices: trunk-based development, code review within one working day, blameless post-mortems, one week in six on call (with a rota bonus)
- We publish our architectural decisions as short ADRs and invite candidates to read two of them before the interview.

**Benefits:** hybrid work, EUR 1,500 learning budget, 28 days holiday, pension scheme, home-office allowance, company-paid language lessons.

I bring 21 years of experience building backend services and distributed systems, with deep experience in Python, including FastAPI and Tornado, Go, PostgreSQL, APIs and high-throughput platforms. My earlier work in fleet telematics also gives me direct experience with transport-related systems: at Nordfels Telematik, I developed backend services ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles.

At Streamhaus, I led the technical development of the playback API and designed a Go entitlement service handling up to 120,000 requests per second. I later led the platform organisation through a migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. Although I have led engineering organisations, I continue to write code every week and remain motivated by designing, implementing, and improving backend services. These projects involved building reliable services at scale and making practical architecture decisions—experience I would bring to Tessel’s event ingestion and tracking APIs.

Tessel’s focus on reliable shipment visibility, clear design notes and engineers taking ownership of services aligns well with the way I have worked. I have used PostgreSQL/PostGIS, RabbitMQ and Kafka, and my experience deploying services on GKE and working with Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry would support Tessel’s focus on cloud operations and observability. I also introduced architecture reviews and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide, and built a Python test harness that was used by QA for eight years.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and transport-systems experience could contribute to Tessel’s Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is focused, professional, and appropriately concise. It opens with a clear match to the role, uses strong quantitative evidence (300,000 vehicles, 120,000 requests/second, 99.5% to 99.95% availability), and connects the candidate’s fleet-telematics background to shipment tracking. The explanation of continued hands-on coding helps address the potential concern that the candidate’s recent Director-level role may be less hands-on. The closing is appropriate and tailored to Tessel’s Routing & Tracking team. The main content limitation is that it emphasizes GCP/GKE rather than directly addressing the job’s AWS environment, although the associated CV lists AWS experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parsable: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional punctuation, no tables or graphics, and includes relevant terms such as Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, APIs, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, RabbitMQ, and transport systems. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the Python backend, distributed systems, logistics/transport, event-driven systems, and observability aspects of the role. Screening strength is somewhat reduced because the letter does not explicitly mention AWS, Docker, REST APIs, CI/CD, query tuning, or schema migrations. Docker, CI/CD, query tuning, and schema migrations are not supported by the supplied candidate information and should not be added merely to match the advert.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with the role’s backend Python, high-throughput API, event ingestion, transport-domain, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, architecture, reliability, and technical-trade-off themes. The fleet-telematics experience is especially relevant to shipment tracking. It also credibly references ownership-related practices through architecture reviews and on-call guidelines. The candidate’s material shows strong Python and PostgreSQL experience, but it does not establish the advert’s specific query-tuning or schema-migration experience. It also does not establish Docker or CI/CD experience, and the letter does not demonstrate REST specifically. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be fixed by rewriting. Dutch or French is not listed; German, Italian, and English are listed. The candidate is substantially more experienced and senior than the advert’s stated target profile, so the letter’s explanation of continued coding is useful and should be retained.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the third paragraph, after the sentence beginning "I have used PostgreSQL/PostGIS," add a carefully bounded reference to the AWS tools listed in the associated CV without claiming unsupported AWS deployment experience. For example: "My broader cloud-platform toolkit also includes AWS (EC2 and S3), alongside GKE, Kubernetes and Terraform." This improves keyword alignment with the advert while remaining truthful. Do not add Docker, CI/CD, query tuning, schema migrations, or REST-specific claims because they are not established in the supplied candidate information.
